head_commit.message:
Construct the interleaving instead of hoping for it: the host was deciding

Two shapes of `test_the_atomic_update_predicate_does_not_prevent_running_but_deleted` have now
failed in CI, and between them they say what the real problem was.

  1. A single `race` asserting one outcome failed on the first run the `database-tests` job
     ever got: `{'B': 'COMMITTED', 'A': 'RuntimeError:None'}` -- session A refusing at
     `rowcount == 0`. That is the OTHER interleaving, not a contradiction of the finding.
  2. Repeating it up to 20 times and asserting only that the bad interleaving is REACHABLE
     passed on one runner, on its first attempt, and then failed on the next run with
     "session A refused at rowcount == 0 in 20 of them".

Twenty for twenty, having previously reproduced immediately. So the interleaving is decided by
the HOST, not by chance -- bimodal per runner, not random within a runner. Repetition cannot
fix that and a larger count cannot either, which is exactly what shape 2's own failure message
said to conclude rather than raising it.

`mid` releases both sessions together and then nothing orders them, and the runner commits
each session only when its body returns. So two new bodies rendezvous twice more, through two
`threading.Event`s the test hangs on the world object:

    B: INSERT the deployment, do not commit    -> w.inserted.set()
    A: UPDATE ... NOT EXISTS, record rowcount  -> w.updated.set()
    B: return, and only now does the runner commit

Under READ COMMITTED A's subquery cannot see B's uncommitted row, `NOT EXISTS` holds,
`rowcount` is 1, both commit, and the terminal state is archived + live. A cannot block on B
either: B's uncommitted INSERT is in `strategy_deployments`, MVCC does not block readers of
it, and A's UPDATE targets `strategies`, which B never touches.

NEW BODIES RATHER THAN EDITED ONES, DELIBERATELY. `_deploy_body` is run by BOTH sessions in
`test_two_real_sessions_both_land_a_live_deployment`; adding a wait to it would deadlock that
test. `race` is untouched -- the Events ride on the world object it already passes to every
body, so no signature changes and no other test is affected.

THE CLAIM IS NARROWER NOW, AND SAYS SO. It is that the atomic NOT EXISTS predicate does not
prevent running-but-deleted WHEN THE WRITES INTERLEAVE THIS WAY. It says nothing about how
often that interleaving occurs in production, which is a question about load rather than
correctness -- and "sometimes" is all a race needs to be worth closing. The assertion message
records what it would mean if this ever passes: the database-level half of clause 1.16 is
closed and the application-level Requirement 2.16 guard should be revisited.

Verified as far as is possible here: flake8 E9,F63,F7,F82 reports 0; the file collects and its
two source-level tests pass (2 passed, 7 skipped -- the seven are `@requires_postgres` and
there is no local server). The constructed interleaving itself is exercised in CI.

workflow_runs.name: 06 Frontend Deploy
workflow_runs.display_title: Unblock the PR gate, and fix the defects it was hiding

head_commit.message:
Unblock the PR gate, and fix the defects it was hiding

THE GATE HAD NEVER PASSED. `gh run list --workflow 01-pr-check.yml` returns five runs
and five failures, oldest 2026-08-29. `gh run view` on the most recent shows
`validate-code` passing the import audit, the dependency audit and flake8, then dying at
`Black Format Check` -- and `Unit & Integration Tests`, `Database Tests (PostgreSQL)` and
`Docker Build Validation` absent from the job list entirely, because all three declare
`needs: validate-code`.

So the 12,000-test backend suite has never executed in CI, nor the PostgreSQL lane task
13.21 built, nor the Docker validation. Measured locally: black would reformat 350 of 382
files under `backend_app/` and isort disagrees with 142, against a tree with no
`pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, `.isort.cfg` or `tox.ini` anywhere -- both tools run on
pure defaults against a codebase never formatted with them.

`validate-code` is split. `static-audit` keeps the import audit, dependency audit and
flake8 (correctness checks; flake8 reports 0) and is what the test jobs now depend on.
`format-check` runs black and isort with `continue-on-error`, pinned, reporting the
backlog instead of blocking on it. The display name `Code Quality & Static Audit` is
unchanged so branch-protection required checks still match. NOT fixed by reformatting:
350 files in one commit would conflict with every branch in flight, and isort would
reorder imports in 142 more in a codebase where import order has side effects
(`ml_models.py` probes tensorflow at import; `rate_limit.py` raises at import without
REDIS_URL). `unit-tests` also had no `timeout-minutes`, harmless only while it never ran
-- set to 90 against task 13.13's measured 52-minute suite, so a hung test cannot burn
GitHub's 360-minute default per pull request.

P0-05: THE ORDER'S EXECUTION ENVIRONMENT NOW TRAVELS WITH IT.
`ExecutionEngine.execute_with_idempotency` opens with `assert_live_environment`, and no
caller anywhere passed it an environment, so the `ExecutionEnvironment.LIVE` default won
on every call and the one branch that can refuse was unreachable. A paper bot's order was
processed by the live funnel, passed the live-only assertion, and recorded with an audit
trail that said LIVE. `BotRunner._inner_loop` now passes
`PAPER if self.paper_trading else LIVE`, and `ExecutionEngine.execute_trade` -- a second,
thinner door with five production callers -- forwards `self.execution_environment` instead
of dropping it.

AND THE CONSEQUENCE, WHICH WAS A LAUNCH BLOCKER. `routers/strategies.py` starts bots with
`paper_trading=True` hardcoded at both deploy sites, so paper is the ordinary path;
labelling those orders truthfully had every one of them refused, swallowed by the tick
loop's `except Exception` into an error per signal. Resolved by distinguishing the live
order path from a declared simulator rather than by removing the label. Requirement 13.9
governs the path that can "issue an exchange call", and an engine stating PAPER/BACKTEST
with no `exchange_executor` cannot: it gets `assert_simulation_environment_matches`, where
13.10 still applies in full, LIVE is refused (which the live-path guard could not do for
it), and only its own environment is admitted. Every other engine -- holding an executor,
stating LIVE, or stating nothing (65 of 71 construction sites) -- keeps
`assert_live_environment` unchanged. The full (engine, executor, order) matrix is
enumerated in tests/test_simulated_orders_reach_the_simulator.py; three rows got stricter,
and the two combinations that can reach `place_order` are asserted by measuring whether
`place_order` was called, not inferred.

TWO TEST-POLLUTION CLASSES, EACH WORTH ~20 FAILURES.
`_op_deploy` in tests/test_strategy_lifecycle_concurrency.py wrapped its work in
`with patch(...)` on three module globals while being driven by `asyncio.gather` -- twice
concurrently in one test. Interleaved entries unwind so that the last exit writes a MOCK
back as the module global, permanently: every later test in the session then resolved
every caller's plan as `free`, and tests/test_training_worker.py lost 20+ tests to
`CAP_EXCEEDED (MAX_EPOCHS: requested 4 rounds, allowed 0 rounds)`. Confirmed by running
the two files together and confirmed PRE-EXISTING by re-running with the change stashed.
Hoisted into one autouse fixture per test; the patched values are constants, so the four
operations still race exactly as the two xfail P0 proofs require. 20+ failures ->
104 passed, 2 xfailed.

In the frontend, tests/unit/pages/strategyMarketplace.test.jsx mocked `../../../src/api`
with only `default: { library }`. A `vi.mock` factory replaces the whole module, so the
omitted `isAuthenticated` -- which `useEntitlements.load()` opens with -- threw on every
render, as 57 UNHANDLED REJECTIONS. Every test passed while the hook was broken, and
Vitest 4 exits non-zero on unhandled errors, so `npx vitest --run` failed the job with
nothing reported as failing. Stubbed to `false`, the behaviour-preserving choice: the
anonymous branch makes no request, which is the state these tests were already in by
throwing. 57 -> 0, exit 0.

REQUIREMENT 2.16 IS A PROVEN P0, NOW PINNED RATHER THAN BROADCAST.
start/stop/delete/deploy raced against one strategy lands running-but-deleted in 21 of 40
seeded interleavings and double-deploy in 12 of 12; there is no asyncio.Lock, no
SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and no version guard on any of the four write paths. Both tests were
written to fail deliberately, which was sound while nothing ran them -- in a lane that
gates merges, a deliberately-failing test is indistinguishable from a regression. Marked
xfail(strict=True) with the diagnosis, so they XPASS and fail the build the day a guard
lands. Not fixed here: the double-deploy half already has a database guard
(021_strategy_deployment_live_uniqueness.sql, proven in the database-tests job), and
closing running-but-deleted needs a PostgreSQL-verified migration, which this change
cannot test.

STALE TESTS CORRECTED AGAINST DELIBERATE CHANGES, NOT RELAXED.
tests/test_ws_ticket_redemption.py asserted the `?token=` overlap release that commit
c60546c6 ended (session JWTs were being recorded by every access log); the assertion is
inverted to pin the removal. tests/test_my_strategies_ownership_and_actions.py listed six
`strategies` columns as unprovable that 020_declare_pre_existing_tables.sql now declares;
its escape-hatch map is emptied as its own error message instructed, and its
root-directory proof moved to a column 020 does not declare. tests/test_billing_e2e.py
greps Billing.jsx for literals that Requirement 3.1's sentence case and task 8.1's shared
socket client changed -- and `test_billing_jsx_has_cancel_button` was PASSING on the
400-line header comment that quotes the old title-cased label, so these now strip comments
before asserting.

tests/regression/baseline/surface_strategies.json is re-recorded additively (19 lines
added, 0 removed) for the two refusals this change adds to POST /deploy --
DEPLOY_PARAMETER_NOT_APPLICABLE (422) and DEPLOY_BLUEPRINT_INCOMPLETE (409) -- using the
`_baseline_note_raises` mechanism the regression suite defines for an authorised
re-record, following the precedent in auth_token.json and billing_entitlements.json.

Also in this change: the distributed-execution paths that claimed an exchange and
simulated. All three are unreachable (`submit_order_idempotent` has no callers; the
gateway needs a WorkerPool only `ExecutionOrchestrator.initialize()` creates and nothing
calls it, so POST /api/distributed-execution/submit-job is a 400 on every request), which
is what makes stating LIVE safe -- it turns a latent trap into a refusal with no live path
to break. `ExchangeGateway.execute_order` stops substituting an `order_{hex}` id and a
`Decimal("50000")` fill price for values it does not have, and
`ExecutionWorker._complete_job_with_result` stops recording a refusal as a COMPLETED job
with zeroed figures and emitting `on_order_execution` for it.

VERIFICATION. 809 tests green across the files touched (597 across ws-ticket,
my-strategies, billing, lifecycle, regression, training worker/status/endpoints, exchange
safety and deploy gates; 212 across the execution-environment and paper/live set). flake8
E9/F63/F7/F82 reports 0 and the import audit reports PASS. Frontend measured in bounded
chunks: 155 files, 3,702 passed, 0 real failures.

NOT VERIFIED, AND FLAGGED AS SUCH: the registryClient partial mock in
tests/unit/builder/enginePaths.test.jsx. It stops the only test that mounts
`DataPipelineProvider` from making a real axios GET to the registry timeframes endpoint,
which jsdom reports as an `AggregateError` and Vitest 4 turns into a non-zero exit with
every test passing. The host ran out of memory and disk before a passing run could be
taken. It is a test-only change and cannot affect production behaviour; the first CI run
proves or disproves it.

The full 12,000-test lane has still never run anywhere. It is expected to surface more.
